key_insight: A reasoning-capable LLM can substantially improve speaker recognition in long TV dramas by using storyline context instead of relying only on local utterances. The paper also introduces a large-scale benchmark that makes this hard task measurable at drama scale.
problem_solved: The paper tackles speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas, where many characters, overlapping dialogue, and long-range story context make it difficult to determine who said each line. Existing methods struggle to connect utterances to the correct speaker across long sequences and many episodes.
method: Build DramaSR-532K, a large benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines spanning 900+ unique characters.
Use a reasoning LLM to infer speaker identity by leveraging broader narrative context, character relationships, and dialogue history.
Evaluate speaker recognition on long-form drama settings where long-range dependencies and ambiguous dialogue are common.
impact: This work shows that LLM reasoning can be used beyond text generation to solve structured video-understanding tasks. For practitioners, it offers a scalable benchmark and a strong direction for building systems that understand characters, dialogue flow, and story context in entertainment media.

paper_title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
paper_authors: Yuxuan Li, Lingxi Xie, Xinyue Huo, Jihao Qiu, Jiacheng Shao
